comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C32-C40 regarding route-dependent efficacy of 3D11. Both evaluations find the dose-response relationship and differential protection between skin and i.v. routes well-supported by Figure 1 data. Reviewers described this as 'convincing in vivo data' and OpenEval noted adequate statistical significance and sample sizes.

Strong agreement on claims C53-C63 regarding intracellular effects on liver stage development. Both identify this as the key novel finding. Peer reviewers highlighted this as 'the only novel yet very important observation' and OpenEval confirmed support through comprehensive flow cytometry and immunofluorescence data in Figure 4. Peer review also notes C88 (temporal patterns) which OpenEval addresses separately in R9.

Agreement on claims C64-C67 regarding UIS4-negative phenotype and mechanistic explanation for late killing. Both evaluations find the immunofluorescence data in Figure 5 convincing. Peer review also includes C89 and C101 which OpenEval addresses in R9 and R11 respectively, showing the mechanistic interpretation is accepted across evaluations.

Agreement on summary claims C98-C100, C102 regarding major findings. Both evaluations confirm these accurately represent the study's contributions. Peer reviewers described the work as 'elegantly designed' and 'important,' while OpenEval noted the claims are supported by comprehensive experimental data.

Agreement on claims C46-C51 regarding motility inhibition and microscopy findings. Both evaluations accept the intravital microscopy data showing reduced parenchyma entry. Peer review also includes C79-C81 (which OpenEval addresses in R8), indicating the connection between these observations and the broader mechanistic understanding.

Agreement on claims C41, C43-C45 regarding temporal kinetics and late-killing effect. Both evaluations find the bioluminescence data in Figure 2 convincing. Peer reviewers specifically highlighted the temporal dynamics as important, and OpenEval confirmed adequate statistical analysis across multiple time points. Peer review also includes C78 and C103 which OpenEval addresses in R8 and R11.

Agreement on claims C85-C86 regarding prior work on late intrahepatic effects. Peer reviewer specifically requested citation of Nudelman et al. (1989) for these claims, which was added. OpenEval found these mechanistic interpretations reasonably supported, though somewhat speculative. Both evaluations recognize the importance of contextualizing findings with prior literature.

Disagreement on claim C13 regarding correlation between antibody levels and protection. OpenEval classified C1-C28 as supported background claims with appropriate citations. However, peer reviewer specifically critiqued C13, noting lack of direct proof of causation and absence of antibody cut-off levels distinguishing protected from unprotected individuals. This represents a substantive disagreement on the strength of evidence for this background claim.

OpenEval evaluated claims C29-C31 regarding established properties of 3D11 antibody as supported by prior publications. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific background claims about the antibody characteristics.

OpenEval evaluated claims C68-C82 integrating findings with prior literature and comparing with other antibodies. While peer review touched on some of these claims (C78-C81 in R3), the comprehensive evaluation of the discussion's integration with literature was not explicitly addressed in peer review.

OpenEval evaluated claims C83-C84, C87, C89 regarding mechanistic interpretations and dose-response similarities. While peer review addressed C85-C86 (R7), C88 (R4), and C89 (R5) individually, there was no comprehensive peer evaluation of this cluster of mechanistic interpretation claims as a group.

OpenEval evaluated claims C90-C97 regarding alternative mechanisms and areas requiring further investigation as supported by appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these discussion claims about alternative mechanisms and future directions.

OpenEval evaluated claim C104 as a reasonable concluding statement about the work's importance, noting it is somewhat speculative regarding future applications. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific concluding claim.
